payload.answer: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026, an acceleration from 0.5 percent growth in the fourth quarter of 2025 (ref-1: "Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026 ... In the fourth quarter of 2025, real GDP increased 0.5 percent."). The second estimate revised Q1 growth down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate of 2.0 percent to 1.6 percent, "primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending" (ref-1: "Real GDP was revised down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending."). This revision is a data update, not a change in actual economic activity: it reflects updated source data (e.g., revised inventory investment "based primarily on revised U.S." data), not a slowdown that occurred in the economy. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, 'GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 1st Quarter 2026,' published 2026-05-28 (ref-1).

citations.quotation: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026 (January, February, and March), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. In the fourth quarter of 2025, real GDP increased 0.5 percent.
Real GDP was revised down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending.

Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent (0.4 percent at a quarterly rate1) in the first quarter, a downward revision of 0.4 percentage point from the previous estimate, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending.

counterarguments.text: The GDP acceleration may overstate underlying momentum: the companion measure real gross domestic income grew only 0.9 percent in Q1 2026 (vs. 1.6 percent in Q4 2025), and the average of real GDP and real GDI was 1.3 percent, suggesting growth was weaker than the headline GDP figure implies.

citations.quotation: 0.9 percent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with an increase of 1.6 percent in the fourth quarter of 2025. The average of real GDP and real GDI increased 1.3 percent, compared with an increase of 1.1 percent.
